workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch and one pull request: implement -> test -> review round 1 (COMMENT, head still carries .legion/) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> review round 2 (APPROVE naming the clean head by SHA) -> retro (revived implementer) -> merger publishes READY -> merge queue merges -> implementer confirms the file on main and records it on the PR and the issue (acceptance 3) -> architect signs off. No build, test suite, formatter, or linter exists in this repository; every check is a command against GitHub whose output is recorded.

implement: legion-worker — the path-limited jj split, the bookmark -r @- push, the PR body READY format with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-134` line, the re-run-not-repush CI rule, rebase only on CONFLICTING, the .legion/ deletion push, and the post-merge production check all come from it.
legion-retro — the same implementer is revived after approval for the mandatory retro (one docs/solutions/ commit, one Dispatch issue comment, no handoff).
dispatch — the post-merge record and the retro comment go on the Dispatch issue with dispatch_comment in plain English, because `legion gh` refuses every GitHub-issue write.
test: legion-worker — defines the E2E section the tester writes (real surface, exact command, observation, head SHA, one negative control with a link) and the handoff commit/push gate.
verification-before-completion — each of the spec's acceptance lines is proven by running the named command and recording its output; the implementer's handoff is never the evidence.
review: legion-worker — one review per round through `legion gh -- api --method POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews` with commit_id; COMMENT while .legion/ is on the head, APPROVE only the clean head named by SHA; CI, threads, and E2E verified on GitHub, never from a handoff; the Thermo line is omitted on this docs-only PR.

concerns: The working-copy commit @ carries the daemon-provisioned, empty .omp/config.yml (snapshot.auto-track = all(); the repository has no .gitignore). It must never reach GitHub. Verified in a scratch jj repo: `jj split -m <msg> <paths>` moves the bookmark to the REMAINDER commit (the new @, which keeps .omp/config.yml and has no description), and `jj bookmark set <name>` without -r targets that same @, after which `jj git push` refuses with 'Won't push commit … since it has no description'. Every phase therefore runs `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-134 -r @-` before pushing. Sibling branches legion/LEGSMOKE-131 and -132 confirm this works. Moving the bookmark from @ to @- is a backwards move: `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-134 -r @- --allow-backwards` is the exact command (without the flag jj refuses: 'Refusing to move bookmark backwards or sideways').
Anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is auto-snapshotted into @. Scratch files (PR body, review JSON, negative-control directory) live under /tmp, never in the workspace.

GitHub main was 373184959b7a62c7e283f131564b8aeaad9365a2 when planned and the file is absent there (contents API returns 404). LEGSMOKE-131 and LEGSMOKE-132 have open PRs (#41 is LEGSMOKE-132) that add different smoke/ files and may merge first; a newer main is NOT a rebase trigger — only `mergeable: CONFLICTING` reported by GitHub is.

Both workflows run on `push` AND `pull_request`, so every head shows FOUR check-runs (check ×2, gate ×2), not two — verified on PR #41 head ad321ac725fa. The `ci` job sleeps 20 s; wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.

Thermo: the PR is a single 78-byte markdown file, i.e. docs-only, so per legion-worker the reviewer runs no thermonuclear pass and omits the Thermo line entirely. The architect may override; if so the reviewer runs both thermo agents once at the round-1 head and adds the line.

Scope tension raised to the architect: the spec and the planner assignment say nothing outside smoke/legsmoke-134.md and .legion/ changes, but legion-retro mandates one docs/solutions/ commit after approval. This plan follows the skills (the docs/solutions/ file is the only path allowed above the approved head; the tester's only-smoke-plus-.legion check applies at the tester's head, before retro). If the architect rules the other way, retro records its learnings only as the Dispatch issue comment and the merger expects an empty `diff --summary` above the approved head.

`legion gh` refuses GitHub-issue writes (`gh issue comment` included); legion-retro's example `gh issue comment` is replaced by dispatch_comment on LEGSMOKE-134. Likewise the acceptance-3 record 'on this issue' is a dispatch_comment.

After the .legion/ deletion push nothing writes a handoff: cleanup, APPROVE, retro, merger READY, and the post-merge confirmation all report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ changes the approved head and restarts the review loop.

The tester and reviewer identities may lack permission to `pr edit` the body (HTTP 403 for a GitHub App that is not the author). Fallback: post the exact E2E line (tester) as a PR comment with the Legion footer and ask the architect to have the implementer paste it into the body with its next push; never leave the evidence only in a handoff.
The repository has no AGENTS.md and no repository-local skills, so the harness skills named in requiredSkills drive every surface.

unchanged → confirmation only: the tester re-checks the bare gates (four check-runs success at the new head) and edits the E2E head SHA with 'rebase re-check <old> → <new>: fingerprint unchanged, bare gates only'; a prior APPROVE gets one confirming APPROVE naming both SHAs. changed → full test round and one new review.

ciFailurePolicy: A failed check-run at any head: read it with `legion gh -- run view <run-id> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --log-failed`. Flaky or infrastructure failure → `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never a new commit. Real failure caused by this change (only possible if `.fail-me` reached the tree, which allowedPaths forbids) → fix in this PR. `ci` cannot fail on content (it only sleeps 20 s).
